title: Opus
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Overworked manga artist Chikara Nagai is about to end his series Resonance by having its villain, Masque, kill the hero Lin, when he is pulled into his own manga. Inside, the characters have become aware of their world and their author, and Masque tries to seize control of the story and become a god. The serialization stopped in the mid-1990s and the work ends unresolved.
life_message: A creator owes something to the people he makes, and must come to see his characters' suffering as real to them.

folkways.japan: The weekly manga serialization system, with tight deadlines and editors pressing for dramatic endings, frames Nagai's situation.

delivery.evidence: AIPT reviewer describes subtle commentary on storytelling and an intellectual, engrossing tone.

personified.ideology: the author's right to do as he likes with his creations

delivery.note: The creator-versus-creation question is raised through events rather than stated, and the unfinished ending leaves it open.

winners_losers: Sympathy goes to the characters who resist being written to death; the author's urge to kill for effect is questioned. The work is unfinished, so no one clearly wins.
